title: It's impossible to move apps grouped in the task manager to another virtual desktop with drag-and-drop
line: Dragging a grouped task from the task manager onto another desktop in the Pager now moves all of its windows there.
explanation: A group in the task manager had no drag data (its MimeData was an unimplemented FIXME) and advertised the plain 'windowsystem/multiple-winids' type, while the Wayland tasks model only accepts its own uuid-suffixed group format and never parsed it either. So the Pager's drop found no windows and did nothing. The grouping proxy now derives the group mime type from its children and carries the children's window ids one per line, and WaylandTasksModel::winIdsFromMimeData() parses that list.

commits.message:
libtaskmanager: allow dragging grouped tasks to another desktop

Grouped tasks offered no drag data and a mime type that Wayland tasks
don't recognize, so dropping a group on the Pager did nothing. Groups now
carry their windows' ids in the Wayland group format, which is parsed.

BUG: 456041

media.caption: Before: dragging the grouped Konsole icon (3 windows) onto Desktop 2 in the Pager does nothing
After: the same drag moves all 3 Konsole windows to Desktop 2
Before: after the drop all 3 Konsoles are still on Desktop 1
After: the Pager tooltip lists the 3 Konsoles on Desktop 2

reviews.text: Clean, minimal fix in libtaskmanager that implements the two long-standing FIXMEs for grouped task drag-and-drop on Wayland. TaskGroupingProxyModel now derives the process-local multiple-winids mime type from its children and joins their window UUIDs, and WaylandTasksModel::winIdsFromMimeData() parses them safely with proper null checks. Autotests pass and the before/after media clearly verify moving grouped windows to another desktop via the Pager.
